text: The young man was Chandragupta Maurya.
His teacher was a sharp, ruthless brahmin called Chanakya, also known as Kautilya.
The story goes that Chanakya had been insulted at the Nanda court and swore he would not
tie up his hair until the Nandas were destroyed.
Rule 1 of ancient India, never insult the guy with the untied hair.
Around 321 BCE, Chandragupta and Chanakya overthrew the Nandas and took Magadha's capital,
Then Chandragupta did what nobody had done before.
He united most of the subcontinent into one state, the Morya Empire, Stitch.
When one of Alexander's generals, Celicus, came to take back the Indian lands, Chandragupta
pushed him out and made a deal, land in the northwest for 500 war elephants.
A Greek ambassador, Megasthenes, lived at Pataliputra and described a huge city of wooden
walls with hundreds of towers and a moat around it.
Chanakya is traditionally credited with the Arthashastra, a handbook on how to run a state,
Scholars still debate who exactly wrote it and when.
